Actual first-person world paints distinct visible WebGL2 pixels
Cockpit has no floating mph/fuel gauges or permanent storage/objective clutter
Driving route card stays clear of the lower cockpit instruments
Automatic quality reduces full-scene backing pixels during sustained active slow frames
Live driving snapshots do not write the career every few seconds
Native keyboard acceleration and steering produce real distance, fuel use and heading changes
Sustained active frames over 250 ms continue bounded simulation rather than freezing it
Settings pause discards held input and does not advance vehicle state
Resuming a paused scene does not repay the unseen pause as a simulation jump
Brake, handbrake and grounded car exit preserve the driven career
Regional map hides the background header and its controls
Regional map uses the real 12 km by 10 km bounds and shows service destinations
Region view keeps complete settlement names inside the map at the small viewport
Nearby view keeps complete settlement names inside the map at the small viewport
Closing the regional map restores the header and hit-tested controls
Save, title and career reload retain vehicle pose, fuel, damage and mileage
Physical pump service hides the background header and its controls
Closing physical pump service restores the header and hit-tested controls
Fuel is purchased at the modeled pump without repairing damage or resetting mileage
Paid repairs restore vehicle condition while keeping fuel and mileage
E prompt matches its action and the car can be re-entered after pump service
Actual T roadside tow charges $150 and preserves fuel, damage, gear and mileage
Final walking movement remains live until the exit checkpoint
Linux development update manager does not block the offline local world
Real native Save and exit flushes the latest movement before app shutdown
A fresh native process reloads the final durable career through the real preload
Reopened career enters and paints the actual saved first-person world
Nearby map clips distant venues and maps the real 2.4 km by 2 km viewport
Reopened nearby view keeps complete settlement names inside the map at the small viewport
Grounded highway, campus and coast scenes paint for regional art and physical wayfinding review
Actual native W driving strikes the deterministic plaza resident and saves severe career penalties
Police response stays pending while settings pause the live scene
Native Save and exit retains the active police response and its immediate penalties
A fresh native process preserves pending police time and every immediate career penalty
Actual resumed fixed simulation advances persistent police response to arrival
Native police resolution preserves penalties and impounds at the nearest service without free repairs, fuel or mileage reset
Native Save and exit retains the resolved incident and impounded vehicle

limitations: Native Linux development build with software SwiftShader; this is not a Mac or Windows native runtime test.
Offscreen window and disabled OS sandbox are confined to the Linux container QA process. Production BrowserWindow security and GPU flags are unchanged.
Mac fullscreen/signature/update installation and Windows installer behavior are not exercised here.
HTTP and HTTPS renderer requests are blocked throughout this isolated fixture; bundled file resources remain available.
Valid synthetic careers are written only into the isolated QA profile. No player career is seeded or replaced.
The test bypasses the single-instance OS socket lock in memory because this Linux container blocks socket creation. Single-instance locking is not exercised.
The headless fixture supplies a fixed cursor position because the headless Linux Ozone surface has no physical pointer. Desktop pointer and monitor selection are not exercised.
A synthetic 1280 by 800 monitor is supplied in memory to the headless fixture. Physical display selection and fullscreen transitions are not exercised.
Native titlebar options are omitted in the offscreen Linux fixture; OS titlebar styling is not exercised.
Pointer capture is unavailable in the offscreen fixture; its request rejects immediately. Native mouse locking is not exercised.

Active slow-frame regression deliberately delays renderer requestAnimationFrame scheduling by 300 ms. The normal grounded/cockpit scene remains visible during all input checks. These are simulation/quality/governor assertions under Linux software rendering, not target-hardware frame-rate measurements.

candidates.name: Maya Chen
candidates.bio: Maintains a payment library after her day job. No degree; thousands of people rely on her code.
candidates.hook: Fixed a race condition that three senior engineers missed.

candidates.name: Theo Mercer
candidates.bio: Left a large agency to build tools for people with limited vision.
candidates.hook: The prototype works with a keyboard alone.

candidates.name: Nia Okafor
candidates.bio: Runs a volunteer repair network with almost no money and very little fuss.
candidates.hook: Coordinated 60 volunteers through a citywide outage.

candidates.name: Elliot Vance
candidates.bio: An impressive list of employers and titles. His portfolio credits large teams.
candidates.hook: Claims to have led a complete platform migration.

candidates.name: Sana Patel
candidates.bio: A quiet final-year student with an unusual eye for interaction design.
candidates.hook: Her unfinished project has a remarkably clear onboarding flow.

candidates.name: Rafael Cruz
candidates.bio: Knows everyone in the local startup scene. Enjoys solving urgent problems.
candidates.hook: His former team grew fast, then missed two launches.

candidates.name: Jun Park
candidates.bio: Automated the family repair shop between customer appointments.
candidates.hook: The inventory tool is faster than the commercial one it replaced.

candidates.name: Amara Bell
candidates.bio: Builds exhibits that make complex ideas accessible to children.
candidates.hook: A visitor figured out the exhibit without reading a word.

candidates.name: Levi Brooks
candidates.bio: A warehouse coordinator who quietly eliminated a major delivery bottleneck.
candidates.hook: The improvement survived after he moved to another shift.

candidates.name: Iris Vale
candidates.bio: Solved every programming challenge, but prefers to work alone.
candidates.hook: Her code is elegant; nobody else could maintain it.

candidates.name: Felix Reed
candidates.bio: A persuasive presenter with a beautifully polished portfolio.
candidates.hook: Every case study looks excellent; user outcomes are missing.

candidates.name: Aisha Noor
candidates.bio: Works reception at a busy clinic. Patients ask for her by name.
candidates.hook: Built a scheduling system that reduced missed visits.
